stances.claim: President Lee Jae-myung's two-day Philippine state visit presents a rare opportunity for Korean partnership with the Philippines in upholding the rule of law and constitutionalism over lawlessness and dictatorship.

South Korea demonstrated profound democratic resilience during the upheaval caused by the unlawful late-2024 martial-law declaration, which led to the impeachment of the sitting president -- CJP was struck by how swiftly democracy recovered from what could have become a fatal crisis, stressing the power of civilians and a new generation viewing martial law as a relic of a bygone era.

South Koreans understood that the rule of law is the strongest safeguard against the caprices of power -- proving beyond a shadow of doubt that a true democracy cannot be ruled by men, but by laws; this is a fundamental lesson on liberty that Filipinos have also learned the hard way over their own democratic history. CJP supports the recent nominations of South Korean citizens for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

Lee Jae-myung's ascent after the upheaval is deeply instructive -- his journey from childhood poverty to human-rights lawyer to the presidency resonates with CJP, who also wrestled with poverty and setbacks before becoming Chief Justice. In his UN speech, Lee quoted Nobel-laureate Han Kang and declared South Korea's return as a 'beacon of light' for democracy and global citizens.

Pursuant to the 2025 APEC summit discussions, the state visit will advance shared priorities through best-practices exchange, the Philippine-Korea Free Trade Agreement, and collaboration in electronics and semiconductors -- industries at the heart of AI integration -- generating jobs, promoting competitiveness, and driving shared growth along an automation-defined economic trajectory.

For the business community, the visit signifies a commitment to productivity and transparency that transcends rhetoric -- invoking ex dolo malo non oritur actio (a right of action cannot arise from fraud or irregularity) and ratio legis (the soul of the law). Investor confidence is a byproduct of stable regulatory frameworks; against the backdrop of Philippine corruption investigations, the path forward requires renewed dedication to institutional integrity, since economic growth and the rule of law are intertwined and mutually inclusive -- judicial credibility reinforces investor confidence, and development that neglects justice becomes brittle.
stances.rhetorical_move: ex-dolo-malo + ratio-legis Latin-maxim anchoring + brittle-development warning

stances.claim: As the Philippines assumes ASEAN chairmanship, bilateral successes with Seoul will serve as a prima facie case for a rules-based regional order -- ASEAN stands at a crossroads navigating great-power rivalries and security tensions, and the challenge is to imbue 'ASEAN centrality' with credibility rooted in shared norms. The Philippines earned global respect when it chose arbitration over arms and stood firmly, with dignity and honor, on the side of international maritime law.

Both nations have learned that constitutionalism is not self-executing -- invoking pacta sunt servanda (agreements must be kept), which applies not only among countries but also between a state and its people. The visit offers an opportunity not merely to celebrate friendship but to recalibrate cooperation anchored on shared constitutional values, democratic resilience, and rules-based development.
Liberty and prosperity are best safeguarded and nurtured when the rule of law governs power, not the other way around.

one_paragraph_summary: Written on the eve of South Korean President Lee Jae-myung's two-day Philippine state visit, the column frames the bilateral encounter as a rare opportunity to forge partnership in upholding the rule of law, constitutionalism, and AI development. Panganiban praises South Korea's democratic resilience during the 2024 martial-law upheaval, endorses the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize nominations for South Korean citizens, and parallels Lee's poverty-to-presidency trajectory with his own poverty-to-Chief-Justice arc. He situates the visit within the 2025 APEC follow-through, the Philippine-Korea FTA, Korean leadership in electronics, semiconductors, and AI (citing Boston Dynamics' Atlas under Hyundai), and the Philippines' incoming ASEAN chairmanship -- recalling that the country earned global respect when it chose arbitration over arms via the 2016 Arbitral Award. Invoking ex dolo malo non oritur actio, ratio legis, and pacta sunt servanda, he closes with the conviction that liberty and prosperity are best safeguarded when the rule of law governs power, not the other way around.
